name: Bourbon
description: American whiskey made mostly from corn. Sweet and round, with vanilla, caramel and oak.

pairsWith.reason: Lemon cuts through the sweetness and lifts the vanilla.
The herbs and dark fruit in vermouth sit well with oak.
A little spice keeps the sweetness in check.

name: Rye whiskey
description: American whiskey made mostly from rye. Drier and spicier than bourbon, with a peppery finish.

pairsWith.reason: Sweet vermouth softens the spice. This pairing is the Manhattan.
Bitters echo the pepper and clove notes already in rye.

name: Blended Scotch whisky
description: Malty and gently smoky, with honey and dried fruit. A blended Scotch is the easiest kind to mix.

pairsWith.reason: Bubbles open up the aroma and make it a long, light drink.
Drambuie is made from Scotch and honey, so the two blend seamlessly.
Ginger adds warmth that suits the malt.

name: Irish whiskey
description: Smooth, light and slightly sweet, with very little smoke.

pairsWith.reason: Its gentle sweetness rounds off the bitterness of coffee.
Ginger and a squeeze of lime make an easy tall drink.

name: Gin
description: A clear spirit flavoured with juniper, which tastes of pine, plus citrus peel and spices.

pairsWith.reason: The bitterness of tonic sharpens the juniper.
Citrus brings out the peel flavours already in the gin.
Vermouth adds a soft, herbal edge. This pairing is the Martini.
Gin is crisp enough to stand up to a strong bitter liqueur.

name: Vodka
description: A clean, nearly neutral spirit. It adds strength without much flavour, so the other ingredients lead.

pairsWith.reason: Fiery ginger gives a neutral spirit something to carry.
Vodka adds strength without getting in the way of the coffee.
Tart fruit juice does the flavour work while vodka stays in the background.

name: White rum
description: A light rum made from sugar cane. Clean and faintly sweet, with a grassy note.

pairsWith.reason: Lime balances the sweetness. Rum, lime and sugar is the base of many classics.
Fresh mint lifts the light, grassy side of the rum.
Tropical fruit suits the sugar-cane flavour.
Cola adds caramel and spice that white rum lacks.

name: Dark rum
description: A rum aged in barrels. Rich, with molasses, toffee and spice.

pairsWith.reason: Ginger heat cuts through the richness.
Lime keeps a rich rum from tasting heavy.
Almond syrup adds a nutty roundness that suits aged rum.

name: Tequila
description: Made from the agave plant. Earthy and peppery, with a citrus note. A clear "blanco" tequila is best for mixing.

pairsWith.reason: Lime sharpens the earthy agave flavour.
Orange liqueur adds sweetness and a citrus aroma. With lime, this is the Margarita.
Grapefruit has a gentle bitterness that suits agave.

name: Brandy
description: A spirit distilled from wine and aged in oak. Fruity and warm, with raisin and vanilla. Cognac is a well-known kind.

pairsWith.reason: Orange brightens the dried-fruit flavour.
Lemon stops a rich spirit from feeling heavy.
Chocolate and brandy make a classic dessert pairing.

name: Orange liqueur (triple sec)
description: A clear, sweet liqueur flavoured with orange peel. Cointreau is a well-known brand.

pairsWith.reason: Sweet orange softens sharp lime.
It sweetens and perfumes tequila without hiding it.
Orange and aged grape spirit are a long-standing match.

name: Amaretto
description: A sweet Italian liqueur that tastes of almond and marzipan.

pairsWith.reason: Plenty of lemon is needed to balance how sweet it is.
Almond and coffee is a familiar dessert combination.

name: Campari
description: A bright red Italian liqueur. Strongly bitter, with orange peel and herbs.

pairsWith.reason: Sweet vermouth tames the bitterness and adds depth.
Soda stretches it into a lighter, refreshing drink.
Orange picks up the peel flavour inside the liqueur.

name: Aperol
description: A light orange Italian liqueur. Like a gentler, sweeter Campari, with only mild bitterness.

pairsWith.reason: Bubbles and a little acidity turn it into a spritz.
A slice of orange matches its main flavour.

name: Coffee liqueur
description: A sweet liqueur that tastes of roasted coffee. Kahlúa is a well-known brand.

pairsWith.reason: Vodka adds strength while the coffee flavour stays clear.
Cream turns it into something close to an iced latte.

name: Drambuie
description: A Scottish liqueur made from whisky, honey, herbs and spices.

pairsWith.reason: It sweetens Scotch and adds honey and spice.
Lemon balances the honey.

name: Chocolate liqueur (crème de cacao)
description: A sweet liqueur that tastes of chocolate and vanilla. It contains no cream despite the name.

pairsWith.reason: Cream makes the chocolate flavour taste like dessert.
Brandy adds warmth and stops it being too sweet.

name: Blackcurrant liqueur (crème de cassis)
description: A dark, sweet liqueur made from blackcurrants.

pairsWith.reason: A small amount turns dry sparkling wine fruity and pink.
Lemon balances the jammy sweetness.

name: Sweet vermouth
description: Red wine strengthened with spirit and flavoured with herbs and spices. Sweet, with a bitter edge. Keep it in the fridge once open.

pairsWith.reason: Its sweetness rounds off spicy whiskey.
It softens Campari and adds herbal depth.
With gin and Campari it makes the Negroni.

name: Dry vermouth
description: White wine strengthened with spirit and flavoured with herbs. Dry and crisp. Keep it in the fridge once open.

pairsWith.reason: A small amount softens gin and adds a herbal note.
It gives a neutral spirit some flavour.

name: Sparkling wine
description: Dry white wine with bubbles. Prosecco, cava or Champagne all work. Choose one labelled "brut", which means dry.

pairsWith.reason: Its acidity and bubbles balance a sweet, bitter liqueur.
Fresh juice softens the wine. This is the Mimosa.
Soft, sweet peach suits light sparkling wine.

name: Angostura bitters
description: A concentrated mix of herbs and spices, used a few drops at a time like seasoning. A "dash" is one quick shake of the bottle.

pairsWith.reason: A few dashes add spice and make whiskey taste less sweet.
Clove and cinnamon notes deepen the vermouth.
Bitters make a sweet soft drink taste more grown-up.

name: Simple syrup
description: Sugar dissolved in an equal amount of water. To make it, stir equal parts sugar and hot water until clear, then let it cool. It keeps for a month in the fridge.

pairsWith.reason: Sweetness balances sour juice. Most sours use the two together.
It takes the sharp edge off lemon.

name: Honey syrup
description: Honey thinned with an equal amount of warm water so it mixes into a cold drink.

pairsWith.reason: Honey and lemon is a familiar pairing; the honey adds a floral note.
Floral honey suits the botanicals in gin.

name: Grenadine
description: A sweet red syrup made from pomegranate. It adds colour and a fruity sweetness.

pairsWith.reason: It sweetens ginger ale and turns it pink.
Lime keeps it from being cloying.

name: Almond syrup (orgeat)
description: A sweet, cloudy syrup made from almonds, with a hint of orange blossom.

pairsWith.reason: Nutty almond rounds out rich rum.
Lime balances the sweetness.

name: Soda water
description: Plain fizzy water. It makes a drink longer and lighter without adding flavour.

pairsWith.reason: It lengthens whisky and opens up its aroma.
It dilutes bitterness into something refreshing.
Lime and soda is a simple, sharp refresher.

name: Tonic water
description: A fizzy mixer that is both bitter, from quinine, and sweet.

pairsWith.reason: Bitter tonic and juniper is the classic match.
Tonic supplies the flavour that vodka lacks.

name: Cola
description: Sweet and fizzy, with caramel, vanilla and spice.

pairsWith.reason: Rum and cola share caramel and vanilla flavours.
Vanilla in the bourbon matches the cola.

name: Ginger beer
description: A fizzy soft drink with a strong, spicy ginger kick. Despite the name, it has no alcohol.

pairsWith.reason: Vodka lets the ginger lead.
Rich rum stands up to fiery ginger.
Lime sharpens the ginger and cuts the sweetness.

name: Ginger ale
description: A fizzy soft drink with a mild, sweet ginger flavour. Gentler than ginger beer.

pairsWith.reason: Gentle ginger adds warmth without hiding the whisky.
Pomegranate syrup makes it fruity.

name: Grapefruit soda
description: A fizzy soft drink that is tart and slightly bitter.

pairsWith.reason: Tart grapefruit suits earthy tequila.
Extra lime makes it sharper and less sweet.

name: Lemon-lime soda
description: A clear, sweet, fizzy soft drink flavoured with lemon and lime, such as Sprite or 7UP.

pairsWith.reason: Bitters add spice and cut the sweetness.
Fresh lime makes it taste less like a soft drink.

name: Cranberry juice
description: Tart, dry and deep red.

pairsWith.reason: Its sharp fruit flavour carries a neutral spirit.
Lime adds freshness to the tartness.

name: Orange juice
description: Sweet and gently acidic. Freshly squeezed tastes much better here than juice from a carton.

pairsWith.reason: Juice softens dry wine and the bubbles keep it light.
Sweet orange softens the pepper in tequila.

name: Pineapple juice
description: Sweet, tangy and tropical. It froths when shaken or blended.

pairsWith.reason: Rum and pineapple is the heart of many tropical drinks.
Coconut makes pineapple rich and creamy.

name: Cream of coconut
description: A thick, sweetened coconut cream sold in tins or squeezy bottles for drinks. Unsweetened coconut cream is different and will need extra sugar.

pairsWith.reason: Tangy pineapple balances the richness.
Light rum adds strength without hiding the coconut.

name: Peach purée
description: Ripe peaches blended smooth. Tinned peaches, drained and blended, work when fresh ones are out of season.

pairsWith.reason: Peach and sparkling wine make the Bellini.
A little lemon keeps the peach flavour bright.

name: Espresso or strong coffee
description: Freshly made and strong. Let it cool for a few minutes before using it in a cold drink.

pairsWith.reason: The liqueur sweetens real coffee and deepens the flavour.
Smooth whiskey and hot coffee make Irish Coffee.
Cream softens the bitterness.

name: Lime juice
description: Sharp and aromatic. Squeeze it fresh: bottled juice tastes flat. One lime gives about 30 ml.

pairsWith.reason: Lime and rum is the classic sour pairing.
Lime brightens earthy tequila.
Lime sharpens ginger and cuts sweetness.

name: Lemon juice
description: Bright and sour, a little softer than lime. Squeeze it fresh. One lemon gives about 45 ml.

pairsWith.reason: Lemon balances sweet, oaky whiskey.
Lemon brings out the citrus in gin.
Honey and lemon balance each other.

name: Mint leaves
description: Fresh and cooling. Use the leaves, not the stalks, and press them gently.

pairsWith.reason: Mint, lime and rum make the Mojito.
Lime keeps mint tasting fresh.

name: Orange slice or peel
description: A slice, or a strip of peel cut with a vegetable peeler. Squeezing the peel over the glass releases fragrant oils.

pairsWith.reason: Orange matches the peel flavour in bitter liqueurs.
Orange oil adds a fresh aroma to whiskey.

name: Egg white
description: Shaken into a drink, it makes a silky foam on top without changing the taste. It is served raw, so use a fresh or pasteurised egg, and leave it out if you are pregnant, elderly or unwell.

pairsWith.reason: Foam softens the sharpness of a sour.
It gives a Whiskey Sour its smooth texture.

name: Cream
description: Double or heavy cream. It adds richness and a smooth texture.

pairsWith.reason: Cream and coffee liqueur taste like a sweet iced coffee.
Cream and chocolate make a dessert drink.

name: Ice
description: Chills the drink and adds a little water as it melts, which is part of the recipe. Use plenty: more ice melts more slowly.

name: Water
description: Used to make syrups from sugar or honey.

name: Sugar
description: Plain white sugar. Dissolve it in an equal amount of hot water to make simple syrup.

pairsWith.reason: Sugar and citrus are the two sides of every sour.

name: Salt
description: A pinch on the rim of the glass makes sour and sweet flavours stand out.

pairsWith.reason: Salt softens bitterness and brightens lime in tequila drinks.

name: Cherry liqueur (cherry brandy)
description: A sweet, dark red liqueur that tastes of cherries and almond. Cherry Heering is the best-known brand.

pairsWith.reason: Cherry sweetness softens the sharp juniper in gin.
Cherry and pineapple are the fruit at the heart of a Singapore Sling.

name: Bénédictine
description: A French herbal liqueur, sweet and honeyed with a hint of spice. Often sold as D.O.M.

pairsWith.reason: A little adds a herbal, honeyed depth to gin.
Herbs and honey round out the fruit.

name: Calamansi juice
description: Juice of the small green calamansi lime. Sharper and more fragrant than ordinary lime, with a hint of orange. Squeeze it fresh.

pairsWith.reason: Its fragrance suits the citrus peel in gin.
Bubbles lift the sharp citrus.
It is very sour, so it needs sweetening.

name: Milo powder
description: A malted chocolate drink powder. Sweet, malty and chocolatey. It contains milk and barley malt.

pairsWith.reason: Milk makes it creamy, as in the drink itself.
Brandy's dried-fruit warmth suits malt and chocolate.

name: Milk
description: Fresh full-cream milk. Lighter than cream, so the drink stays easy to sip.

pairsWith.reason: Cold milk and Milo are a kopitiam classic.
Milk softens strong coffee.

name: Sweetened condensed milk
description: Thick, very sweet tinned milk. It sweetens and adds creaminess in one spoonful. Stir it into something warm so it dissolves.

pairsWith.reason: It is what makes local kopi sweet and creamy.
It hides the burn of a neutral spirit.

name: Gula Melaka syrup (palm sugar syrup)
description: Palm sugar melted into a syrup. It tastes of caramel with a hint of smoke. To make it, chop the palm sugar, stir it into an equal amount of hot water until dissolved, then let it cool. It keeps for a month in the fridge.

pairsWith.reason: Caramel and smoke suit the toffee notes in aged rum.
Palm sugar and coconut are the taste of chendol.

name: Rose syrup
description: A bright pink, very sweet syrup scented with rose. Sold in bottles in most supermarkets.

pairsWith.reason: Milk softens the sweetness and turns it into Bandung.
Soda makes a simple pink fizzy drink.

name: Evaporated milk
description: Unsweetened tinned milk with some of the water removed. Creamier than fresh milk and lighter than cream.

pairsWith.reason: Together they make Bandung.
It is the milk in a kopi C.
